result.title: Detection Augmented Learning In Non-Stationary Bandit Environments
result.comment: 36 pages, 1 table, 5 figures, extension of https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19401
result.summary: We study the problem of non-stationary bandits without knowledge of the environmental changes. We propose Detection Augmented Learning (DAL) a black-box paradigm that comprises three modular components: a bandit algorithm, a change detector, and a forced exploration schedule. This modular design enables its applicability across a broad spectrum of bandit problems, from classical to highly structured settings. First, we provide theoretical insights into DAL's strong empirical performance: a single regret bound shows that DAL transfers the regret of its stationary input to the piecewise stationary setting, attaining or improving the best known bounds in every setting considered. We further identify conditions under which DAL performs well in drifting environments. Then, we showcase DAL's practical performance and versatility through extensive experimentation in which DAL consistently surpasses all state-of-the-art methods, both prior-free and prior-based, across diverse non-stationary scenarios in nine bandit settings. Finally, we investigate the effectiveness of the forced exploration and show that a bandit-driven strategy improves performance and shortens detection delay.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Detection Augmented Learning 这一黑盒模块化框架，将 bandit 算法、变化检测器与强制探索策略组合，用于未知环境变化下的非平稳 bandit；给出把平稳设定 regret 迁移到分段平稳设定的界，并在九类设定上做实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「检测到分布变化才触发再探索、并由算法驱动缩短检测延迟」的思路，可能与 LVR 中判断内部状态或缓存失效、进而决定是否重新获取视觉证据（LOOK/STOP 触发条件）的问题有概念类比，可供核查。
